description: Return the largest nonnegative integer not representable by a bounded coprime set of denominations.

source.title: Numerical Semigroups: Apéry Sets and Hilbert Series
source.implementation_status: bounded clean-room Apéry residue shortest-path profile

output.encoding: max(Ap(S,a))-a, where Ap(S,a) stores the least representable value in each residue modulo a=min(coins)

contract.definition: The Frobenius number is the largest nonnegative integer not expressible as a nonnegative integer combination of the supplied denominations.
contract.primary_method: Dense Dijkstra over residues modulo the minimum denomination; every denomination c creates an edge r -> (r+c) mod a with edge weight c; return the greatest shortest distance minus a.
contract.independent_method: Boolean unbounded reachability dynamic programming over every amount from zero through 224; scan the proven finite interval for the final unreachable amount.
contract.invalid_cases: Null, malformed length, m outside 2..4, length not equal to m+1, denomination outside 2..16, repeated denomination, or gcd other than one returns -1.
contract.bound_proof: a=min(coins)<=15. Each residue is reachable because gcd(coins)=1. A shortest residue path is simple and has at most a-1 edges of weight <=16, so max Apéry distance <=16(a-1)<=224. Thus F<=16(a-1)-a=15a-16<=209, attained by {15,16}. Every amount >=224 is representable.
contract.distinction: The result is a semigroup gap maximum over all amounts, not a minimum-coin or combination count for one target amount.

complexity.primary_time: O(m*a^2), with at most 15 residue selections and 60 edge relaxations
complexity.primary_space: O(a), using fixed arrays of 16 signed 64-bit distances and 16 visited bytes
